simple: This page shows how to make your own matchmaking rules on the Creator Dashboard. You can change how much the built-in signals matter, add your own custom signals, or both. Custom signals need custom attributes first, like a player's skill level saved in a data store. You can test your rules on pretend servers and then apply them to the places in your game.
analogy: It is like adjusting the sliders on a music equalizer. Turn up the bass (ping) and the song (server choice) changes, and you can preview it before you save.
keyPoints: Start on the Creator Dashboard: pick your game, then go to Configurations > Custom matchmaking.
On the Configuration tab, click Create Configuration, give it a name, change signal weights, then Save Configuration.
Choose which places use the configuration, then click Save Configuration again.
To add your own signal, click Add Custom Signal. You can have up to 2 custom signals per game.
Custom signals need a custom attribute first. Each game can have up to 5 player attributes and 5 server attributes.
Player attributes read from a data store. You tell matchmaking which data store, the key template (with `{UserId}`), the value path, and the scope.
Server attributes only need a name, data type, and default value.
Click Preview and Test to see three mock servers scored with your weights. The winner is highlighted.

terms.configuration: A saved set of signals and weights that decides how servers are scored for a place.
terms.custom signal: A scoring rule you make yourself from a custom attribute, like matching players with similar skill.
terms.aggregate: Combine many players' values into one number for the server.
terms.average: Add all values and divide by how many. Skills 10, 20, 30 average to 20.
terms.median: The middle value when sorted. For 10, 20, 90 the median is 20, even though the average is 40.
terms.sum: All values added together, including the joining player's. Used to aim for a total, like team power near 5000.
terms.cluster: Put players with the same value together, like same guild.
terms.diversify: Mix players with different values, like different classes on one team.
terms.data store key template: A pattern for the key where each player's data is saved. With `Player_{UserId}`, a player with ID 42 is stored at `Player_42`.
terms.value path: Where to look inside the saved data. If the data is a table with a `Skill` field, the path points to that field.
terms.scope: An extra name that groups data store entries. If you leave it empty, it is `global`.
terms.mock server: A pretend server used only for previewing scores. It does not reflect real servers.

watchOut: Trying to add a custom signal before making a custom attribute. Create the attribute first on the Attributes tab.
Forgetting the second Save Configuration after picking places. Your configuration will not be applied otherwise.
Using the wrong data store key template. It must match exactly how your scripts save player data, or matchmaking cannot find it.
Treating preview scores as real. They come from pretend servers, so also check the Analytics tab after you go live.
